gen-gf-gabarito-gf-antic-slab: Gabarito looks drawn with a single nib, its terminals cut open so the counters flow outward. Antic Slab, a serif with round bowls and wide, barely curled s curves, carries a longer read with a dignified, editorial steadiness.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-arvo: Arvo reads as a traditional serif, dignified, with curves that refuse to close around themselves. And Gabarito keeps every line monoline from stem to serif, expressive up top, while Arvo does the quieter work of settling into text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-belgrano: Gabarito draws its bowls at stem thickness, expressive and distinctive, with terminals cut open. Belgrano, a text serif with open-mouthed curves that stay clear, supplies the classic, traditional counterweight, and that difference is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biorhyme: BioRhyme reads bookish and refined, its curve ends stopping like brush strokes lifted early, its capitals widely spaced. Gabarito gives each line a smooth, tube-like look above it, so a longer passage in BioRhyme feels like turning pages under a bold title.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biorhyme-expanded: Refined, bookish and wide-set. Gabarito brings a blueprint-lettering feel of constant line, expressive and distinctive, while BioRhyme Expanded keeps its open e and generous gaps for the running text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biz-udmincho: Wire-bent sign lettering, constant in thickness, with terminals cut open so the counters flow outward: that is Gabarito. BIZ UDMincho, a text serif with shallow terminal curl, handles the bookish, traditional reading.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-copse: Gabarito has no swelling in its bowls, so every letter looks drawn with one nib and opened outward. Copse, a classic serif with visible daylight through every curved opening, brings a literary warmth, and that mix of expressive and classic is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-cutive: Cutive reads refined and literary, its wide tracking and generous c opening giving running text real breathing space. But Gabarito's lines keep their width through every turn, and that crisp, expressive contrast is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-david-libre: Gabarito is expressive, with strokes that never pinch at the curves. David Libre, a dignified serif with terminals that hang open, gives a longer page a refined, settled texture beneath that lively heading.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-enriqueta: Gabarito leads with stroke ends that look cut from the same ribbon, expressive and distinctive, its counters flowing outward. Enriqueta follows in chalky, literary serif curves that stop well before closing, dignified across a long read.
